 St. Francis House launches ‘Healing Home’ campaign to expand Sioux Falls campus 
 By Alex Duus Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 12:33 PM CST | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (Dakota News Now) - St. Francis House is asking Sioux Falls businesses to help raise $1.5 million toward a campus expansion for people moving out of homelessness.
 The organization has officially launched its “Healing Home” fundraising campaign through the Greater Sioux Falls Chamber of Commerce Community Appeals program. The Chamber portion is part of a $10 million campaign goal needed to complete the project.
 Ben Dold, president and chief operating officer of Midco, and Mark Millage, director of community relations at Furniture Mart USA, are leading a group of more than 60 volunteers who will seek donations from Chamber members over the coming months.
 The project adds 38 efficiency units. It also adds dedicated space where community partners can offer on-site services, including:
 behavioral health care 
 substance use recovery programs 
 healthcare 
 employment assistance 
 financial counseling 
 cultural support 
 The campus will also include the community’s first Donation Depot. It is designed to give residents an easy way to donate goods to St. Francis House and its partner nonprofits.
 “The Healing Home Campus is built around responsible stewardship,” said campaign co-chair Ben Dold. 
 “We are bringing partner agencies together, allowing each organization to contribute its expertise while sharing programming, resources, and in-kind donations.”
 Local officials say St. Francis House plays a key role in the region.
 “St. Francis House provides services and care that are unmatched in our region. The organization has a long-standing presence in the Sioux Falls community as one of the lead agencies that steps forward and takes a proactive approach to meet the needs of those impacted by the criminal justice system,” said Kari Benz, director of human services for Minnehaha and Lincoln counties.
 One guest described the impact of St. Francis House this way:
 “They helped me get myself back on my feet and financially stable by helping me find a job. Staff help keep me from the streets and keep me sober. Without this place, I wouldn’t be where I am today.”
 Campaign leaders say stories like that are how they will measure success.
 “The greatest reward will not be the buildings we construct,” said campaign co-chair Mark Millage. 
 “It will be seeing people heal, families reconnect, individuals return to the workforce, and people who once experienced homelessness or incarceration become stable and contributing members of our community.”
 The Healing Home Campus Capital Campaign Kickoff event runs from 4:30 pm to 6:00 pm on Wednesday, November 4, at the Mosaic in Sioux Falls.
 To learn more about St. Francis House or to donate, visit www.stfrancishouse.com .
